# @allons-y/webc-code-sample

> `norn-code-block`: a WebC code sample highlighted at build time. Shiki runs during the build. The browser gets token ranges for the CSS Custom Highlight API and a copy button, and no highlighter. The reference at the end is generated from the component source.

## What you are working with

- One component, `norn-code-block`, and one Markdown add-on, `highlightFences`.
- It is an optional peer of `@allons-y/webc-patterns`. Installed beside it, the Norn plugin registers the component, the `nornTokenRanges` helper, and the add-on, and the Norn layouts show their code with it. Without it, the plugin registers a plain `norn-code-block` that renders `<pre><code>`, so every call site works either way.
- It registers nothing itself. Do not add it to a project's WebC `components` list when the Norn plugin is in use.

## Use it

```html
<norn-code-block @language="js" @caption="example.js" @code="const answer = 42;"></norn-code-block>
```

- Props take the `@` prefix. `@code` is required and holds the code as a string. `@language`, `@caption`, and `@chrome` are optional. The component has no default slot for code.
- In Markdown, a fenced block becomes a `norn-code-block` with the fence's first word as `@language`. Write fences as normal.
- Every visitor-facing text is a named slot: `label` (names the code when there is no caption), `copy-label` (names the button; `{name}` stands for the code's name), `copy`, `copied`, `failed`. An empty slot falls back to the site's `componentStrings`, then English.

```html
<norn-code-block @language="sh" @code="npm install">
	<span slot="label">Commande d'installation</span>
	<span slot="copy">Copier</span>
</norn-code-block>
```

## Rules

- An unknown or empty language renders plain, readable text with no highlighting. Use `loadLanguages` from the package to register more Shiki languages at build time.
- Theme the colors with the shared tokens (`--norn-code-keyword`, `--norn-code-string`, `--norn-code-flag`, and the rest of the `code` group) in the project's own stylesheet. The component has no custom property of its own.
- `@chrome="terminal"` frames the code with a flat header bar for the caption. It is a prop, not a custom property.
- `data-tokens` is an implementation detail: a compact group table plus integer triples. Read it with `decodeRanges` if you must. Do not write it by hand.
- Highlighting needs the CSS Custom Highlight API. A browser without it shows the code as plain text.

## Where to look next

- README: install, usage without the Norn plugin, translating, layout requirements.
- Component preview: https://allonsy-studio.github.io/webc-resources/

## Reference

Generated from the component sources and their CSF files. Do not edit by hand: run `yarn llms`.

### Component components

A self-contained element: a link, a code block, a lockup.

#### norn-code-block

Tag: `<norn-code-block>`.

Code sample tokenized at build time. Its script registers `norn-code-block` as a custom element that adds the highlight colors; without the script the markup is the whole sample. A compact `norn-copy-button` from `@allons-y/webc-patterns` sits over the top end corner of the code, as its icon until the pointer or focus is on it, and copies the code without any leading `$ ` prompts. While the button shows, the code scrolls in an area that stops short of it, so no code runs beneath it. A caption, when there is one, sits above the code. The code reads left to right in any page direction. While the code scrolls sideways, the script makes it a tab stop, so a keyboard can scroll it. Shell samples (`sh`, `bash`, `shell`, `shell-session`) color the command, its subcommand, its flags, and its arguments apart. Needs `tokenRanges` registered as the `nornTokenRanges` JavaScript function, and the patterns package's components. The names and the copy button's texts are in the page, hidden: the script names the code while it scrolls, and shows the button. Each falls back to the site's `componentStrings`, under `norn-code-block` for `label` and `copy-label` and under `norn-copy-button` for the rest, then English.

Props:

- `code` (string, required): The code to show.
- `language` (string, optional): A language Shiki has loaded: the defaults or one added with `loadLanguages`. Unknown or empty renders plain text.
- `caption` (string, optional): Also names the code and its copy button.
- `chrome` (string, optional, one of `terminal`): `terminal` frames the code with a header bar for the caption. Without it the code sits on its surface with the caption above.

Slots:

- `label`: The code's name without a caption, as one element. Falls back to "{language} code", with the language filled in, or "code" with no language.
- `copy-label`: The copy button's name, with `{name}` for the code's name, as one element. Falls back to "Copy {name} to clipboard".
- `copy`: The copy button's text. Falls back to "Copy".
- `copied`: The copy button's text after a copy. Falls back to "Copied".
- `failed`: The copy button's text when the copy fails. Falls back to "Copy failed".

Global tokens it reads: `--norn-ui-border-radius`, `--norn-ui-icon-s`, `--norn-surface-raised`, `--norn-surface-code`, `--norn-text-muted`, `--norn-font-mono`, `--norn-font-size-s`, `--norn-code-text`, `--norn-code-punctuation`, `--norn-code-comment`, `--norn-code-string`, `--norn-code-keyword`, `--norn-code-function`, `--norn-code-number`, `--norn-code-flag`, `--norn-space-2xs`, `--norn-space-xs`, `--norn-space-s`, `--norn-space-m`.
